_comment: Model-by-model HIGH-complexity eval set (RL-2026-06). EXACT same 5 specs across every model — normal product prompts, NOT benchmark tasks. Stacks are named explicitly so cross-model diffs measure the model, not stack roulette. Each spec demands tests so the TESTS scoring slot fires.

prompts.title: Multi-tenant project/task SaaS API (Spring Boot)
prompts.spec:
Build a multi-tenant project-management REST API in Spring Boot 3 (Java 21, H2 in-memory DB, JPA).

Domain: Organization, User, Project, Task, Comment. Users belong to one organization; projects belong to an organization; tasks belong to a project with status (TODO/IN_PROGRESS/DONE), priority, assignee, due date; comments belong to tasks.

Requirements:
1. JWT auth: register + login endpoints; every other endpoint requires a valid token.
2. Org-scoped RBAC with roles ADMIN, MEMBER, VIEWER — ADMIN manages users/projects, MEMBER creates/edits tasks and comments, VIEWER is read-only. A user must NEVER see or mutate another organization's data (cross-org requests return 403).
3. Invitation flow: ADMIN invites an email with a role; the invite token is used at registration to join that org with that role.
4. Activity feed endpoint per project (created/updated/status-changed events, newest first, paginated).
5. Task list endpoint with filtering (status, assignee, due-before) + pagination + sort.
6. Consistent JSON error envelope (code, message, details) with bean validation on every request body.
7. OpenAPI/Swagger annotations on all endpoints.
8. Tests: integration tests proving the RBAC boundaries (VIEWER cannot mutate, MEMBER cannot administer, cross-org access 403s) plus happy-path CRUD, and unit tests for the invitation logic. Include a README with run instructions.

prompts.title: Realtime collaborative Kanban (Node + WebSocket + React)
prompts.spec:
Build a realtime collaborative Kanban board: Node.js (Express) backend with the `ws` WebSocket library and SQLite persistence, plus a React frontend.

Requirements:
1. REST CRUD for boards, columns, and cards (title, description, labels, position).
2. Drag-and-drop reordering of cards within and across columns. Reordering uses optimistic concurrency: every card carries a version; a stale-version mutation returns 409 and the client refetches.
3. WebSocket sync: every mutation (card create/update/move/delete, column changes) is broadcast to all clients viewing that board; clients apply patches without a full reload.
4. Presence: each board shows who is currently viewing it (name + color chip), updated live as clients join/leave.
5. WebSocket reconnect with backoff on the client, resyncing board state on reconnect.
6. React frontend: board view with columns, draggable cards, presence strip, and a simple card-edit modal. Keep styling minimal but clean.
7. Tests: unit tests for the reorder/position logic and the optimistic-concurrency conflict path, plus a test for the broadcast fan-out (can use a mocked socket layer). Include a README with run instructions for backend + frontend.

prompts.title: Config-driven ETL pipeline CLI (Python)
prompts.spec:
Build a config-driven ETL pipeline as a Python CLI tool.

Inputs (generate realistic sample files as part of the deliverable): products.csv (sku, name, category, unit_price_usd, currency) and orders.jsonl (order_id, sku, qty, unit_price, currency, country, ts — one JSON object per line, including some malformed rows and FX currencies like EUR/INR).

Requirements:
1. YAML config file declaring sources, validation rules, transform steps, and output target; the CLI reads everything from it (no hardcoded paths).
2. Validation with per-row error quarantine: malformed/invalid rows go to quarantine.jsonl with a machine-readable reason; the pipeline NEVER crashes on bad rows.
3. Transforms: join orders to products on sku, normalize all amounts to USD via a configurable FX table, compute line_total and order-level totals, flag anomalies (qty <= 0, price deviating >50% from catalog price).
4. Idempotent + resumable: a checkpoint file records processed order_ids; re-running skips them; --resume continues an interrupted run; --dry-run validates without loading.
5. Load to SQLite (orders, order_lines, anomalies tables) and emit a summary report (rows in/out/quarantined, revenue by category, top-5 products, anomaly count) to stdout and report.json.
6. CLI flags: --config, --resume, --dry-run, --verbose.
7. Tests: unit tests for validators, FX normalization, anomaly detection, and checkpoint/idempotency behavior. Include a README with run instructions.

prompts.title: E-commerce checkout service with payment webhooks (Node/Express)
prompts.spec:
Build an e-commerce checkout backend in Node.js (Express, SQLite).

Requirements:
1. Catalog + cart: endpoints to list products (seed ~10), and create/update a cart (add/remove/charge quantities) with server-side price calculation.
2. Inventory reservation: starting checkout reserves stock with a 15-minute TTL; expired reservations are released by a background sweep; overselling must be impossible even with concurrent checkouts.
3. Idempotent order creation: POST /orders honors an Idempotency-Key header — the same key returns the same order, never a duplicate charge or double-decrement.
4. Mock payment gateway: an internal module that 'charges' asynchronously and then calls the service's webhook endpoint with an HMAC-SHA256-signed payload (shared secret).
5. Webhook endpoint: verifies the HMAC signature, rejects stale timestamps (>5 min) and replayed event ids (nonce store), and transitions the order on success/failure events.
6. Order state machine: PENDING -> PAID -> FULFILLED, with REFUNDED reachable only from PAID/FULFILLED and CANCELLED only from PENDING; illegal transitions return 409. Refund endpoint triggers a refund through the mock gateway.
7. Tests: idempotency (same key twice = one order), webhook signature verification (tampered payload rejected; replay rejected), reservation expiry, and full state-machine transition coverage. Include a README with run instructions.

prompts.title: Log analytics + alerting service (Python FastAPI)
prompts.spec:
Build a log ingestion and alerting service in Python with FastAPI and SQLite.

Requirements:
1. POST /ingest accepts a batch of log events (service, level, message, ts, optional fields); validates and persists them; malformed events are rejected per-item with reasons while the rest of the batch succeeds.
2. Sliding-window aggregations: per-service event counts and error rates over 1-minute and 5-minute windows, computed incrementally (not a full table scan per query).
3. Alert rules engine: rules live in a YAML config (e.g. error_rate > 0.2 over 5m for service X, or count of level=FATAL >= 1 over 1m). A background evaluation loop checks rules every 10 seconds. Fired alerts respect per-rule cooldown (no re-fire within cooldown) and dedupe (one active alert per rule+service until resolved).
4. GET /query: filter logs by time range, service, level, text contains; paginated.
5. GET /alerts: active alerts and alert history with fired/resolved timestamps.
6. Alert resolution: when the rule condition clears, the alert auto-resolves on the next evaluation tick.
7. Tests: unit tests for the window math (counts/error-rate correctness at boundaries), rule evaluation incl. cooldown and dedupe, and per-item ingest validation. Include a README with run instructions.
